proposals.premise: Five entrance steps make access the first uncertainty, so this direction leads with the step-free courtyard route and the real entry photograph.
proposals.opening: Desktop shows route guidance beside the photograph; phone shows guidance first, then the door, bells, and curb. Hours and quiet hour share this opening.
proposals.move: The first control, “Show step-free entrance,” reveals the library courtyard route, bell, and indoor chairs. A volunteer request then displays the chosen arrival time beside the 30-minute notice.
proposals.tradeoff: Visitors gain immediate physical reassurance, but ordinary walk-in access receives less visual emphasis.

proposals.premise: Because visitors can simply arrive, this direction leads with open access while separating optional volunteer help from any suggestion of booking.
proposals.opening: Desktop pairs “Just arrive” with today’s 09:00–17:00 doors and 13:00–14:00 quiet hour; phone stacks them above two entrance choices.
proposals.move: The first control, an arrival-time field under optional volunteer help, displays the chosen time in the request summary and states that requests must be sent 30 minutes before arrival.
proposals.tradeoff: The low-pressure walk-in message becomes unmistakable, but the step-free photograph and courtyard instructions sit one step lower.
